# Compute and Electricity: What Ten Times More Public AI Capacity Would Require

> In 2024 data centres used around 2.1 TWh, or 3.6% of Swiss electricity. By our estimate, a tenfold increase in public compute based on Alps would require 0.6 to 0.8 TWh per year: manageable with planning, but not as an afterthought.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/rechenkraft-und-strom/ · Published: 2026-11-08 · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

Switzerland's data centres consumed around 2.1 terawatt hours of electricity in 2024, 3.6% of national consumption. By 2030 the Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE) expects 2.5 to 3.2 TWh, and 3.5 TWh in its maximum scenario. The country's largest public AI computer, Alps at CSCS in Lugano, drew around 7.1 megawatts during its official performance measurement. By our estimate, ten times as much public compute with today's technology would require 0.6 to 0.8 TWh per year, i.e. just over 1% of today's final consumption.

<!-- more -->

---

## Methodology

We combine three official or primary sources: the SwissEnergy/SFOE study on the electricity consumption of data centres (May 2026), the SFOE's 2025 electricity balance and the measured power draw of Alps in the TOP500 list (7,124 kW, Level 3 measurement). Alps comprises 10,752 NVIDIA GH200 superchips in 2,688 nodes (CSCS).

The projection for a tenfold increase is **our own estimate** with deliberately simple assumptions: continuous operation for 8,760 hours per year at the measured Linpack power, scaled linearly. For cooling and building services we assume a 30% surcharge (PUE 1.3); this is an assumption, not a measured value for Alps. Newer chips deliver more computing power per watt, so the estimate is more of an upper bound for "ten times Alps".

---

### Data centres are growing, but predictably

Between 2019 and 2024, data centre consumption rose from 1.77 to 2.1 TWh, by an average of 3.4% per year. The growth comes from the large commercial data centres (44% of consumption), whose demand could more than double by 2030. In-house corporate data centres (56%) are stagnating or declining as workloads move to the cloud. The SFOE puts the remaining efficiency potential at around 0.8 TWh, almost 38% of today's consumption.

---

### The starting point on the grid

In 2025 Switzerland generated 67.5 TWh of electricity, with final consumption of 58.0 TWh (up 0.8% on 2024). 55.5% came from hydropower, of which 31.3 percentage points from storage power plants, 27.2% from nuclear energy and 11.8% from photovoltaics. The annual balance, however, says little about winter: data centres run all year round at an almost constant load, including when domestic production is scarce.

---

### What a tenfold increase would cost, in electricity

Calculation (estimate): 7.124 MW × 8,760 h gives around 62 GWh per year for Alps. Ten times that is 71 MW and 0.62 TWh; with a 30% cooling surcharge, 93 MW and 0.81 TWh. This corresponds to 1.1 to 1.4% of final consumption in 2025, less than the increase the SFOE already expects for all data centres by 2030 in its high scenario (+1.1 TWh), and roughly as much as the efficiency potential of existing data centres identified by the SFOE. For comparison: according to the International Energy Agency, a typical AI data centre consumes as much electricity as 100,000 households, and the largest ones under construction twenty times as much.

---

## What this means for policy

- **Plan energy and compute together.** A public AI programme of the order of 70 to 90 MW is feasible for the Swiss grid, but it needs fixed sites with grid connection, cooling and waste-heat recovery. This belongs in the same planning as the expansion of winter production: [Energy & Infrastructure Resilience](@/energy-resilience.en.md).
- **Realise efficiency first.** The identified efficiency potential of around 0.8 TWh in existing data centres corresponds roughly to the estimated demand of a tenfold increase in public compute. Binding efficiency metrics for large data centres free up room on the grid.
- **Expand public compute measurably.** Report targets and progress in megawatts and computing power, with open access for universities, SMEs and the administration: [Sovereign AI & Compute](@/souveraene-ki.en.md).
